title: Medium exam 2
about: Ten single-choice questions that combine two facts or ask you to trace two or three steps: exit codes, redirections, masks, file times and the keys of `less`.

questions.title: Stop the script if the copy fails
questions.text: A script must copy `a` to `b` and, only if the copy fails, print `copy failed` and end with exit status 2. Which snippet does it?

options.why: The block after `&&` runs when `cp` succeeds, the opposite of what is wanted.
With `;` the message and the `exit 2` run always, even when the copy worked.
The block after `||` runs only when `cp` returns a non-zero status.
The pipe does not test anything: `echo` runs anyway, and so does `exit 2`.

questions.title: Showing a password hash
questions.text: You are the normal user `ana`, who is allowed to use `sudo`. Which command shows the line of `/etc/shadow` that holds the password hash of `ana`?

options.why: `/etc/shadow` is readable only by root, so this fails with "Permission denied".
This line has an `x` in the password field: the hash is not stored there.
`sudo` runs `grep` as root, who can read the file.
`/etc/group` lists groups and their members; it has no passwords of users.

questions.title: Searching inside less
questions.text: You open a long file with `less`. The word `main` appears on lines 12, 80 and 140 only. You press `G`, then type `50g`, then type `/main` and Enter. Where are you?

options.t: On line 12, the first line that contains `main`.
options.why: A forward search starts at the current position, not at the top of the file.

options.t: On line 80, the first match after line 50.
options.why: `G` goes to the end, `50g` jumps to line 50, and `/` searches forward from there.

options.t: On line 140, the last match, because you pressed `G` first.
options.why: The `50g` moved you back to line 50 before the search.

options.t: On line 50, because `50g` has fixed the position.
options.why: `/main` then moves to the next line that contains the word.

questions.title: Two sed in a pipe
questions.text:
What does this print?
```
printf 'one two\ntwo two\nthree\n' | sed 's/two/2/' | sed '/three/d'
```

options.why: Without the `g` flag only the first `two` of each line changes.
The first `sed` replaces the first `two` of every line and the second one deletes the `three` line.
The `d` command deletes the lines that contain `three`.
The first `sed` changes the lines; the second one does not undo that.

questions.title: At the GRUB prompt
questions.text: At the `grub>` prompt you want to hand control to the boot loader of a Windows installation, instead of loading a Linux kernel. Which command does that, after the right partition has been selected?

options.why: `linux` loads a Linux kernel image; it cannot start another loader.
`initrd` loads the initial RAM disk of a Linux kernel.
Chain loading passes control to the loader found in the first sector of the selected partition.
That only selects the partition; nothing is started until `chainloader` and `boot`.

questions.title: The order of the redirections
questions.text: `ls /nope /etc/hostname 2>&1 > f | wc -l` is run. What happens?

options.t: It prints `0`, and `f` contains the error message and the listing.
options.why: Redirections are read from left to right, so the error does not follow the output to the file.
The listing goes to `f`: stdout was redirected there after `2>&1`.

options.t: It prints `1`, and `f` contains the listing of `/etc/hostname`.
options.why: `2>&1` copied stdout, which was the pipe, so the error goes to `wc`; then `> f` sends only stdout to the file.

options.t: It prints `1`, and `f` contains the error message.
options.why: It is the other way round: the error goes through the pipe and the listing to the file.

options.t: `mkdir d` creates a directory with the mode `rwxr-xr-x`.
options.why: True: 777 minus 022 is 755.

options.t: `touch f` creates a file with the mode `rw-r--r--`.
options.why: True: files start from 666, so the result is 644.

options.t: `touch f` creates a file with the mode `rwxr-xr-x`, as the directories.
options.why: False: new regular files are not created with execute permission; they get 644.

options.t: The group and the others cannot write in the new files and directories.
options.why: True: 022 removes `w` for the group and for the others.

questions.title: Classifying processes
questions.text: Which statement about the types of process is FALSE?

options.t: A command typed in a shell and run with `&` is still an interactive process.
options.why: True: it belongs to the shell, in the background.

options.t: A script started by the scheduler at 03:00 is a batch process.
options.why: True: it was planned for a given moment.
True: it works in the background doing a task of the system.

options.t: A daemon stops when the user who started it closes the terminal.
options.why: False: daemons are not tied to a user's terminal; they run for the system.

questions.title: Modification time only
questions.text: `notes.txt` has an old access time and an old modification time. Which command changes only its modification time to now?

options.why: `-a` changes the access time only.
Without options both times are updated.
`-m` changes the modification time only.
`-c` means "do not create the file if it does not exist"; the times are updated as usual, both.

questions.title: Numbers in text and in arithmetic

options.why: `$a+$b` is not arithmetic: the shell just puts the two texts around a `+`.
Inside `$(( ))` the `*` multiplies, it does not join the texts.
Inside `$(( ))` the `+` adds the numbers.
Only `$(( ))` does arithmetic; variables are strings otherwise, and inside it `a` and `$a` are the same variable.
